title: Commercial Pilot License Cost
question: What is the all-inclusive cost for a Pilot License?
answer: While training quotes typically state base tuition ($35,000 - $65,000 depending on the program), true all-in budgets must account for Class 1 medical renewals, aviation uniform/equipment, ECAA/ICAO exam fees, accommodation, living stipends, and buffer flight hours. We build a clear 18-month cashflow forecast tailored to your family's budget.

title: International Accreditation
question: Are flight training academies internationally accredited?
answer: Yes. Accredited flight training academies operate as ICAO Training Centers and ATOs authorized under CAA, FAA, and EASA guidelines, training commercial pilots for international carriers.

title: Job Placement Prospects
question: What are the job placement prospects post-graduation?
answer: The global aviation industry faces a forecasted shortage of 600,000+ pilots and technicians over the next 20 years. Graduates with ICAO-standard pilot certifications transition into regional and international airlines.

title: Student Safety & Welfare
question: How is student safety and welfare monitored abroad?
answer: Partner flight academy campuses operate secured gated grounds with full-board student catering, health facilities, dormitories, and international student welfare support.

title: Academic Requirements
question: What are the academic requirements for Cadet Pilot Training?
answer: Applicants must typically have completed high school (Grade 12) with strong passes in Mathematics, Physics, and English (minimum 'B' or equivalent), or hold a university degree in STEM fields. International certificates like Cambridge A-Levels or IB are fully accepted.

title: Vision & Glasses Rules
question: Can I fly if I wear glasses or contact lenses?
answer: Yes! As long as your vision is correctable to 20/20 (6/6) with glasses or contacts and you possess normal color vision and depth perception, you can pass the Class 1 Medical examination.

title: Age Limit for Training
question: What is the age limit to start pilot training?
answer: Minimum age to hold a Private Pilot License is 17, and 18 for a Commercial Pilot License. For commercial flight training, candidates starting from 18 years can enroll and progress directly through their ratings.
